author: DamiLee
description:
Tong lau are the old shophouses you see all over Hong Kong, with a shop at street level and families packed above. They were overcrowded and badly kept, and people got exploited left and right.

They filled up fast after the war. Hong Kong went from around 600,000 people to over 2 million by 1951, and loads of them lived and worked in tong lau. In 1955 the rules loosened, so they could go up to eight or nine floors. If you want to see one up close, go to Lui Seng Chun in Mong Kok. It was built in 1931 with a herbal medicine shop downstairs and the family living upstairs. While you can still find some tong lau buildings in Hong Kong, many of them are being torn down for 40-storey towers.

Would you miss them or is it time they went?

title: The Buildings That Built Hong Kong
